cells.note: `/plan [description]` enters plan mode; adding a description starts that task immediately in plan mode.
`/plan` optionally takes inline text as the first planning request (e.g. `/plan Propose a migration plan`); unavailable while Codex is already working.
Restricted agent mode: file edits and `bash` default to "ask" rather than being blocked outright, via the permission system.
On by default only on select Claude models (Opus/Sonnet 4.x, Haiku 4.5, Claude 3.x); others need it enabled via `--allowedTools`.
Same model-gated availability as task creation; `TaskList` lists all tasks, `TaskGet` fetches one task's full details.
Updates a task's status, dependencies, or description, or deletes it; same model-gated availability as task creation.
Can't be combined with `--base`, `--commit`, or a custom prompt — pick exactly one review target.
Can't be combined with `--uncommitted`, `--commit`, or a custom prompt — pick exactly one review target.
`--title` only works together with `--commit`. Can't combine `--commit` with `--uncommitted`, `--base`, or a custom prompt.
Exactly one of `--uncommitted`, `--base`, `--commit`, or a custom prompt is accepted — they're mutually exclusive.
Pages long files with a PARTIAL notice; also renders images, PDFs (up to 20 pages per call), and Jupyter notebooks. Reads files only, not directories.
Overwrites the entire file (no append or merge); overwriting an existing file requires reading it first.
Exact string replacement only, no regex or fuzzy matching; the file must be read first.
File-edit permissions come from sandbox mode, approval policy, and writable-roots config — there's no separate `apply_patch` permission setting.
Only supported GPT models get `patch`; other models get `edit` and `write`.
Edits one notebook cell at a time by `cell_id`, with replace, insert, or delete modes; insert requires a `cell_type`.
Capped at 100 results. Ignores `.gitignore` by default; set `CLAUDE_CODE_GLOB_NO_IGNORE=false` to respect it.
Uses ripgrep syntax; skips gitignored files unless you pass that file's path directly.
Runs background language servers (pyright, gopls, etc.) and feeds diagnostics into checks after `write_file`/`patch`. Only active inside a git worktree; servers must be installed first.
A built-in set of read-only commands runs without a permission prompt; other commands prompt unless auto-approved.
The default foreground timeout is two minutes; set `timeout` in milliseconds to change it.
`shellPath` sets the shell executable Pi runs commands with (e.g. a Cygwin bash on Windows). Supports a leading `~` for the home directory; unset by default.
`shellCommandPrefix` is prepended to every shell command Pi runs, e.g. `shopt -s expand_aliases` to enable shell aliases. Empty by default.
Returns a `session_id` and `pid` for the process; manage it afterward with `process` (list/poll/wait/log/kill/write).
Shows processes started with `terminal(background=true)` in the current session; other sessions can't see them.
Reads captured output and exit status; readable only from the session that started the process, even with the exact process ID.
Sends input to a running background process (e.g. answering a y/n prompt). Interactive tools need PTY mode (`pty=true`).
Shows each background terminal's command plus up to three recent output lines. Only populated when `unified_exec` is in use — otherwise the list is empty.
Tests `.rules` files against a command without running it; accepts repeated `--rules <file>` flags and prints JSON (`--pretty` for readable output). Experimental.
Resumes the most recent chat in the current directory; add `--all` to include sessions from other directories.
Resumes by ID or name, or opens a picker if none given; alias `/continue`. A session already running can't be resumed this way.
`/resume` (or `pi -r` at startup) opens a picker of previous sessions for the current project. Sessions auto-save under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.
Accepts a session UUID or a session name; if both could match, the UUID takes precedence.
Resumes a previous session by ID or title. `--resume latest` resumes the most recent session scoped to the current workspace (same as `-c`).
Resumes a prior non-interactive run; `--last` picks the most recent session in the current directory, `--all` searches across directories.
Aliases: `/branch` and `/duplicate`.
`/branch [name]` splits a new session off the current point and switches you into it, keeping the original intact; return with `/resume`.
`/fork` creates a new session file starting from a chosen earlier user message, separate from `/tree`, which navigates within the same file.
`/tree` jumps to any earlier point in the same session file and continues from there without creating a new file. Leaving a branch can summarize it first.
`/fork [prompt]` copies the conversation into a new background session while the original keeps running; a prompt starts it working right away.
Hides the session from the picker without deleting its transcript. Supports `--remote` for a remote app-server endpoint.
Restores an archived session to the picker by ID or name; supports `--remote` for a remote app-server endpoint.
`/export [filename]` saves the conversation as plain text; without a filename it offers a dialog to copy or save it.
Opens the transcript in your editor; `opencode session export` writes JSON instead.
`/export [file]` saves the session as an HTML file (or JSONL). Also works headlessly via `pi --export <in> [out]`.
`/export [file]` can save the session as JSONL instead of HTML; also available headlessly via `pi --export <in> [out]`.
Accepts a JSON file or URL; `--directory` imports into another project.
`/import <file>` loads and resumes a session from a JSONL session file.
Imports chats and setup from another tool; scans up to 50 chats from the last 30 days. Available only in the local TUI.
Interactive turn-by-turn undo timeline with per-turn diffs; you can restore just the conversation or files too. Aliases `/undo`, `/restore`.
Lists or restores filesystem checkpoints (`/rollback [number]`, `/rollback diff <N>`). Checkpointing is off by default — enable with `checkpoints.enabled: true`.
Rewinds the conversation and/or code to an earlier point, or summarizes from a chosen message; aliases `/checkpoint`, `/undo`. Also opens via Esc Esc.
Restores both the conversation and file changes from a previous turn, including image attachments. Aliases `/undo`, `/restore`.
Loads memory files from the working directory and every parent directory at launch (project, user, enterprise), concatenating rather than overriding.
`AGENTS.md` loads from `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (global), parent directories, and the current directory. Loads even without project trust, unless `--no-context-files` is set.
Place `AGENTS.md` in the project root (or `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` globally); run `/init` to scan the repo and generate or update it.
Rule files in `.claude/rules/` with a `paths` field load only when you read a matching file; rules without `paths` load every session.
`@path/to/import` in a memory file pulls in another file's contents; imports nest up to 4 levels deep and are skipped inside code blocks.
Adds text to the end of the default system prompt rather than replacing it.
`--append-system-prompt <text>` adds text to the default system prompt for one run; context files and skills are still appended. File equivalent: `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`.
Replaces the entire default system prompt, including built-in tool guidance and safety instructions.
`--system-prompt <text>` replaces the default system prompt for one run; context files and skills are still appended. File equivalent: `SYSTEM.md`.
Shows a colored grid of current context usage with a per-item breakdown; pass `all` to expand it in fullscreen mode.
`/compact [instructions]` summarizes the conversation to free up context, optionally focused by your instructions; `/clear` starts fresh instead.
`/compact [prompt]` manually compacts history, optionally with instructions to focus the summary. Stays available even if auto-compaction is disabled.
Sets the token threshold that triggers automatic compaction; unset uses the model's default. A companion `_scope` key (default `total`) picks full context vs. growth since the last compaction.
`compaction.reserveTokens` (default 16384) sets the token threshold that triggers auto-compaction, and also caps how long the summary itself can be.
`compaction.keepRecentTokens` (default 20000) controls how much recent history stays uncompacted when compaction runs.
When navigating with `/tree`, Pi can offer to summarize the branch you're leaving and carry that summary into the new branch. These are in-session branches, not Git branches.
On by default: Claude saves notes across sessions automatically. Toggle with `/memory`, or disable via `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`.
Off by default; enable with `[features] memories = true` in `config.toml`. Generates memories in the background, respecting rate limits — avoid storing secrets in them.
Stores agent notes and a user profile separately across sessions. Loaded once at session start, not refreshed mid-session; each store can be disabled independently.
`memory_read` is a tool added by the pi-memory extension (not built into Pi) that reads any memory file or lists daily logs.
`memory_write` is a tool added by a memory extension (not built into Pi) that writes to `MEMORY.md` or a daily log.
`memory_search` is a tool added by a memory extension (not built into Pi) that searches memory files by keyword, semantic, or deep mode; requires `qmd`.
Lets you enable using existing memories separately from generating new ones (or keep both off). Files live under `~/.codex/memories/`; secrets are redacted.
Off by default. When enabled, interactive CLI writes prompt you inline; writes from messaging, scripts, or background runs are staged for later review instead.
Reviews writes staged by the `memory.write_approval` gate; only useful when that gate is enabled. Works in both the CLI and the messaging gateway.
When `true` (default `false`), sessions using MCP tool calls, web search, or tool search are excluded from memory generation.
Set in a subagent's frontmatter to give it persistent memory, scoped to `user`, `project`, or `local`.
Spawns a subagent with its own separate context window; use `claude agents` or `--agent` from the terminal to monitor or run one.
Spawns an isolated subagent for parallel work. Concurrency, iteration limits, spawn depth, and model are set under the `delegation.*` config namespace, not this tool name.
Built-in read-only subagent for fast code search, keeping exploration out of the main context; runs once per call and returns no agent ID.
Runs in its own context window with a faster model, executes multiple searches in parallel, and returns only relevant findings.
One of three built-in subagents (General, Explore, Scout); invoke with an @ mention for read-only codebase exploration.
Boolean frontmatter field in a custom subagent's markdown file (default `false`); set `true` to run it in the background without blocking the parent.
Restricts which tools a subagent can use, as a comma-separated string or YAML list; omit it and the subagent inherits every available tool.
Default: 250 tool-calling turns per child agent.
Experimental and off by default; enable with `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` and describe the team in natural language.
`/batch <instruction>` splits large changes into 5-30 units, each handled by its own background subagent in an isolated worktree with tests and a PR; needs a git repo.
Fans out child tasks from the current task. Requires the `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` env var or the kanban toolset — not enabled by the `all`/`*` toolset wildcard.
Pauses the task and surfaces a question to the user; execution resumes once they reply. Requires `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` or the kanban toolset.
Marks the task done with a structured handoff payload (results, artifacts, follow-ups). Requires `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` or the kanban toolset.
`/model [model]` switches models and saves the choice as default for new sessions; with no argument it opens a picker, press `s` to switch just this session.
Keybind `ctrl+x m`.
`/scoped-models` picks which models appear in the `Ctrl+P` quick-switch list. The persisted setting is `enabledModels`, same as the `--models` flag.
`/effort [level]` sets reasoning effort (low to xhigh, plus max/ultracode/auto); which levels are available depends on the model and provider.
`--thinking <level>` sets reasoning effort for the run (off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max). Persist with `defaultThinkingLevel` or per-model `modelThinkingLevels`.
`--fallback-model sonnet,haiku` tries models in order if one fails; persist a chain with `fallbackModel` in settings. Capped at 3 models.
Defines a custom provider's base URL, wire API, and auth/headers. Can't reuse built-in IDs `openai`, `ollama`, or `lmstudio` — use `openai_base_url` to retarget the built-in OpenAI provider.
Runs Codex against a local model server such as Ollama or LM Studio. Pick the provider with `--local-provider` or `oss_provider`; without one, the TUI prompts you but `codex exec` errors.
Requires a running local Ollama server (`http://localhost:11434/v1`); tool calls may need `num_ctx` increased.
`pi.registerProvider(name, config)` lets a trusted extension add or override a model provider.
Only applies when using OpenRouter as the provider; set via `provider_routing` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. Has no effect on Nous Portal or direct provider connections.
`claude mcp add --transport stdio <name> -- <command> [args...]` runs an MCP server as a local process; add `--scope project` or `--scope user` to share it.
Configured with command/args/env/cwd. Set `required = true` to fail startup if the server can't initialize; `experimental_environment = "remote"` runs it through a remote executor.
Configured with a `url` plus optional auth, bearer token, or headers. OAuth login/logout only works if the server supports OAuth.
Runs a configured MCP server's OAuth flow from the shell without opening the `/mcp` panel; use `--no-browser` to print the URL over SSH.
Authenticates a server listed in `.cursor/mcp.json` (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json`) via OAuth when the server requires it.
Set to `false` to disable a server without deleting its config. Optional (non-required) servers get a 1000ms startup grace period by default.
Also stops the server from prompting for approval, not just from loading.
Searches for and loads deferred MCP tools on demand; only active when MCP tool search is enabled.
`enabled_tools` allow-lists tools from a server; `disabled_tools` is applied afterward, so a tool in both lists ends up disabled.
Resources are also browsable by typing `@` to autocomplete them, rather than calling this tool directly.
Resources referenced with `@` mentions are fetched and attached automatically.
Server-provided prompts appear in the `/` menu as `/servername:promptname`, or run as `/mcp__servername__promptname` with space-separated arguments.
Prompt templates are Markdown files invoked as `/<filename>`, loaded from `~/.pi/agent/prompts` (global) or `.pi/prompts` (project, needs trust); support arguments.
Skills load on demand: only their names/descriptions sit in the system prompt, and the full `SKILL.md` loads when a task matches. Project skills need trust first.
Skills register as `/skill:name` commands (toggle with `enableSkillCommands`, default on). Text typed after the command is passed to the skill.
Browse with `/skills`; invoke with `/skill-name` (supports `-p` print mode) or via Option/Alt+Enter Custom Mode.
Set `context: fork` in a skill's frontmatter to run it in a new subagent with no access to the prior conversation; runs in the background by default.
Re-scans skill and command directories so changes on disk apply without restarting; reports how many were added or removed.
`/reload` reloads keybindings, extensions, skills, prompts, themes, and context files without restarting.
`pi.registerTool(definition)` lets a trusted extension add a custom tool the model can call. Tool output should stay under roughly 50KB/2000 lines.
Defined as TypeScript/JavaScript files, though the tool itself can shell out to any language. Can execute arbitrary code, governed by permission settings.
`pi.registerCommand(name, options)` lets a trusted extension add a user-invoked slash command.
Load from a local directory or npm (auto-installed via Bun) in sequential order. Use `--pure` to skip external plugins, or `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS` to skip default ones.
`ctx.ui.custom()` temporarily replaces the editor with an extension-built UI component until it calls `done()`. Works in the terminal UI only; degraded in RPC mode.
Tools can define `renderCall`/`renderResult` to customize how their calls and results are shown in the terminal UI. Not sent to RPC clients.
Fires when a session begins or resumes; MCP-tool hooks on this event are skipped since MCP servers aren't up yet at launch.
Fires when a session ends; handlers share a 1.5-second budget by default, raisable per-hook up to 60 seconds.
Fires before Claude processes a submitted prompt; default timeout is 30 seconds, so a stuck hook stalls the session.
The `tool_call` extension event can block a tool before it runs by returning `{ block: true, reason?, terminate? }`.
Fires immediately when a permission decision is needed; the related Notification hook only fires after about 6 seconds.
Fires before context compaction with trigger type, token/context counts and message counts; observational only, it can't block or alter compaction.
The `session_before_compact` extension event exposes the messages about to be summarized and lets an extension cancel compaction or supply its own summary.
The `session_before_fork` extension event can cancel a session fork before it happens.
Replaces Claude Code's default `git worktree` creation logic, e.g. to check out an SVN/Perforce copy instead; the hook must print the created path or startup fails.
Pi asks to trust a project folder before loading its local settings, resources, skills, and extensions. It's a loading guard, not a sandbox on what tools can do afterward.
`/trust` saves a trust decision to `~/.pi/agent/trust.json` for future sessions. It doesn't apply to the current session — restart Pi for it to take effect.
Holds allow/ask/deny rules per tool plus mode settings like `defaultMode` and `additionalDirectories`; a deny rule at any scope can't be overridden elsewhere.
Set under the `permission` key in `opencode.json`; most actions default to allow, but `doom_loop` and `external_directory` default to ask, and reading `.env` files is denied by default.
Configure globally in `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` or per-project in `.cursor/cli.json`; e.g. deny `Read(.env*)` to protect secrets.
Works in print mode too; unattended writes there need `--force` and/or explicit permission entries.
Rules live in `.rules` files (Starlark `prefix_rule` entries) deciding whether a command runs unsandboxed, prompts, or is blocked. Project rules load only when `.codex/` is trusted. Experimental.
Starts the session with a classifier model reviewing actions instead of prompting; needs a supported model and org enablement, otherwise falls back to Manual mode.
Beta. Inherits from another profile or the built-in `:read-only`/`:workspace` profiles; extending `:danger-full-access` is rejected, as are unknown parents or cycles.
Sandboxes shell commands on macOS, Linux, and WSL2 with per-command network approval; toggle with `/sandbox`. Falls back to unsandboxed execution with a warning if unavailable.
Beta. Maps paths to read/write/deny access, with optional per-subpath overrides. A missing or empty table keeps filesystem access restricted and prints a startup warning.
No external destinations are allowed until you add allow rules (deny wins on conflicts). The proxy itself must be turned on via `features.network_proxy.enabled` (off by default).
OpenShell runs the whole Pi process inside a sandboxed gateway (Docker, Podman, VM, or remote Kubernetes) with filesystem/network/process controls. A separate external tool, not built into Pi.
Starts Claude in an isolated git worktree at `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`; accepts an issue number or PR/MR URL to branch from, plus `--tmux` for a tmux session.
Creates a worktree under `~/.cursor/worktrees/<repo>/<name>`; requires a Git repository and is disabled for multi-root workspaces. Isolates files locally, not a cloud runtime.
Only applies together with `--worktree`; defaults to the current HEAD if omitted.
Up to 8 backend searches per call, with `allowed_domains`/`blocked_domains` scoping; capped at 200 calls per session by default (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION`).
Converts the page to Markdown and summarizes it with a small model against your extraction prompt, so you get an answer rather than the raw page; cached for 15 minutes.
Governed by the `permission.webfetch` key in `opencode.json`.
Allow entries auto-approve fetches to trusted domains without prompting.
Auto-launches or attaches to a local Chromium-family browser via CDP. Interactive-CLI only — not usable from messaging gateways. Exposes your logged-in browser session to the agent.
Must be called before any other browser tool. Without a CDP connection or cloud provider, Hermes drives its own bundled Chromium rather than your installed browser.
Returns a text accessibility tree with element references (e.g. `@e1`) instead of a screenshot. Truncates around 15,000 characters by default; adjust with `browser.snapshot_threshold`.
Clears the field first, then types the new text.
Handles native JS dialogs (alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload); only active when a CDP endpoint is reachable at session start. Default policy requires an explicit response.
Reads console logs/errors and can evaluate JavaScript on the page. Works on any backend; `browser.restrict_evaluate: true` can block evaluating sensitive data (cookies, storage, clipboard).
Requires Chrome to be connected; then Claude can read console output and errors to help diagnose problems.
Screenshots the page and analyzes it with a vision model — useful for CAPTCHAs or layouts a text snapshot misses. Adds extra inference cost; screenshots are cached for 24 hours.
Research preview, macOS only, off by default: lets Claude open apps, click, type, and see the screen. Needs a Pro/Max plan, claude.ai login, and Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions.
Controls the desktop without moving your cursor, stealing keyboard focus, or switching virtual desktops/Spaces. Requires the external `cua-driver` on PATH; not available on API-server surfaces.
Attach one or more images to the initial prompt: separate paths with commas or repeat the flag, e.g. `codex --image before.png,after.png`.
Paste an image with `Ctrl+V` (`Alt+V` on Windows) or drag it into the terminal; image files can also be passed with `@path`. Inline rendering depends on the terminal.
Opt-in — not loaded by default. Enable with `--toolsets video` or add `video` to your toolsets config.
Uses `gpt-image-2` and counts toward usage limits — consumes included limits about 3–5x faster than plain turns. For larger batches, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` to route through the API.
Generates or edits images via a backend you configure (FAL.ai, OpenAI, xAI, Krea), needing the matching API key/OAuth — unless you're a paid Nous Portal subscriber, which needs no separate key.
`/voice [hold|tap|off]` toggles voice dictation; requires a Claude.ai account.
Push-to-talk voice conversation (`Ctrl+B`) with speech recognition and streaming text-to-speech. `/voice tts` speaks replies to every message; identical behavior in classic CLI and TUI.
`/loop [interval] [prompt]` repeats a prompt while the session stays open; omit the interval to self-pace, omit the prompt to run the built-in maintenance prompt or your `loop.md`.
Schedules a one-shot or recurring prompt within the current session; restored on `--resume`/`--continue` if not yet expired.
Runs without a permission prompt.
Cancels a task created with task scheduling, by ID.
`hermes cron` manages jobs (create/edit/list/pause/resume/run), but automatic dispatch runs in the Gateway scheduler, which checks jobs every 60 seconds.
`/schedule` (alias `/routines`) sets up routines that run in the cloud, not locally, through a conversational setup flow.
Subscribes to events for event-driven activation, delivering to log/Telegram/Discord/Slack/GitHub. Requires the webhook platform enabled in config; `--deliver-only` skips the LLM entirely.
`claude --channels plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` opts into push notifications from an MCP server at startup (research preview); requires claude.ai or Console API key authentication.
Delivers replies at-least-once with bounded recovery; ambiguous sends can appear as visibly labeled duplicates. No cross-platform parity or uptime guarantee.
Requires setting up a bot account and an allowed-user list before it can be used.
Sends a desktop notification, and a phone push if Remote Control is connected, so long-running tasks can reach you.
Requires a connected Remote Control session; not available on Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry.
Runs the agent across many prompts in parallel from a JSONL dataset, mainly to generate tool-use trajectories for fine-tuning/eval. Invoked as `python batch_runner.py`, not a `hermes` subcommand.
Matches already-completed prompts by their actual text content, not by index, so resume works even if the dataset order changes. Failed prompts are retried, not skipped.
Alias `codex e`. Requires a git repository unless you pass `--skip-git-repo-check`. Exits with an error if an enabled MCP server fails to initialize.
Can attach to a running `opencode serve` instance with `--attach`.
Includes session ID and a per-model cost breakdown; cost figures are client-side estimates and may differ from your actual bill.
Streams newline-delimited JSON events, not just the final answer. Pair with `--output-last-message` to also get a plain final-message file.
Choose `text`, `json`, or `stream-json` for print-mode output; several other flags require `stream-json`.
Validates the final response against a given JSON Schema in print mode; exits with an error if the response doesn't match.
Validates the final response against a JSON Schema file you provide; doesn't constrain intermediate tool events.
Short flag `-o`. Writes the final message to a file while still printing it to stdout; combine with `--json` for JSON progress plus a plain summary file.
Stops a print-mode run once API spend hits this dollar cap; subagent spend counts toward it, but it's a client-side estimate, not a hard billing stop.
Limits agentic turns in a print-mode run and exits with an error once reached; unlimited by default.
`pi --mode rpc` runs Pi headlessly, exchanging a JSON protocol over stdin/stdout for embedding in other apps or IDEs. Some terminal-UI-only extension methods are degraded here.
Optional HTTP basic auth: set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` (username defaults to `opencode`, override with `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME`).
Experimental, not for production. Use plain `ws://` only for localhost or SSH-forwarded connections, `wss://` otherwise. `--remote-auth-token-env` supplies a bearer token from an env var.
Hidden from default command help; runs over stdio with JSON-RPC, intended for custom ACP clients rather than normal terminal use.
Flags: `--cwd`, `--port`, `--hostname`, `--mdns`, `--mdns-domain`, `--cors`.
Install with `npm install @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (bundled with the main package) to embed Pi's agent loop from Node.js code.
Official SDKs for Python (`claude-agent-sdk`) and TypeScript embed the agent loop, tools, sessions, and hooks in your app; other languages run the CLI as a subprocess.
Starts a server with no local interactive session, so you can control it from Claude.ai or the Claude app instead.
`/reload` reloads keybindings, extensions, skills, prompts, themes, and context files without restarting Pi.
Starts with all customizations disabled for troubleshooting; authentication, model selection, built-in tools, and permissions still work normally.
Disables all customizations for troubleshooting — user config, memory/rules injection, plugins, shell hooks, and MCP servers. Different from `--toolsets safe` (read-only tools); both can be combined.
Checks for duplicate installs, PATH issues, broken settings, and unused skills/MCP/plugins, then asks before changing anything.
`hermes doctor --fix` attempts automatic repairs, but custom-provider config problems are only reported as warnings and aren't auto-fixed.
Manages the Gateway as a background service (install/start/stop/status/restart) instead of a one-shot CLI process; setup differs between Linux systemd and macOS launchd.
Shows session cost, plan usage, and activity stats; on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise it breaks down what counts against plan limits. `/cost` is an alias.
Flags: `--days`, `--tools`, `--models`, `--project`. Figures depend on the session/provider usage metadata that was recorded.
Exports metrics, logs, and optional traces (beta) covering usage, cost, and tool activity, configured via OTLP environment variables.
Defaults to `none` — events are recorded but nothing is sent until you set `otlp-http` or `otlp-grpc`. Trace and metrics exporters are configured separately (metrics defaults to `statsig`).
Set `PI_TELEMETRY=0` or `enableInstallTelemetry: false` to turn off the anonymous install/update ping and provider attribution headers. Update checks still happen.
Off by default; gateway-only. When enabled, hashes identifiers (phone numbers, user/chat IDs) in the model-visible context on supported platforms — display names stay visible.
`Ctrl+J` and a trailing `\` work everywhere by default. `Shift+Enter` needs a terminal with extended key reporting (e.g. iTerm2); on Windows Terminal, `Alt+Enter` is intercepted for fullscreen.
`Ctrl+J` works in every terminal, including tmux; `Shift+Enter` depends on terminal support. Both insert a newline without submitting.
Pasting a multiline block sends the full text once you press Enter — the compact preview line only summarizes size, it doesn't replace what's sent.
Pasting a large block shows a compact summary like `[pasted: 47 lines, 1,842 chars — press Enter to send]` instead of dumping it into scrollback. Full text is still sent.
`Ctrl+G` opens an external editor for the prompt. Uses the `externalEditor` setting first, then `$VISUAL`, `$EDITOR`, Notepad on Windows, or `nano` otherwise.
Toggle per session with `/vim` (saved as preference), or set persistently via `editor.vimMode` in `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`. Applies to the input area only.
`/vim` toggles Vim mode for the current session only; set `tui.vim_mode_default = true` in `config.toml` to make it the default for new sessions.
Enable via `/config` → Editor mode, or set `editorMode: vim`, for vim-style NORMAL/INSERT editing of your prompt.
Clears the unsent prompt if nothing is running; press again to exit Claude Code.
Installed skills automatically become slash commands too, and commands are case-insensitive (`/HELP` works like `/help`).
After `Ctrl+R` search, press `Enter` to reuse the matched prompt (`Esc` cancels). Separate from draft history, browsed with Up/Down.
Searches prompt history; press `Enter` to use a match or `Esc` to cancel. Separate from draft history, which uses Up/Down.
Interrupts a running operation; if nothing is running, it clears the prompt instead.
`Escape` stops the running agent and puts any queued messages back into the editor.
Pressing `Enter` while the agent works queues a steering message, delivered once the current turn's tool calls finish (not instantly).
Press `Enter` while Codex is working to inject new instructions into the current turn, instead of waiting for the next one.
Injects your message at the next tool-result boundary rather than immediately. Falls back to `queue` behavior if the agent hasn't started yet or images are attached.
Default behavior when you message while Hermes is working — stops the current turn immediately and starts on your new message.
Configurable via `display.busy_input_mode` (default: `interrupt`); works in both the interactive CLI and the messaging gateway.
Pressing `Enter` while the agent works adds a steering message to the queue; delivery timing is set by `steeringMode`.
`Alt+Enter` while the agent works queues a follow-up message, delivered only after all current work finishes.
Press `Tab` while Codex is working to queue a prompt, slash command, or shell command for the next turn.
`steeringMode` (default `one-at-a-time`) controls whether queued steering messages are sent all at once or one at a time.
`followUpMode` (default `one-at-a-time`) controls whether queued follow-up messages are sent all at once or one at a time.
`Alt+Up` pulls a queued message back into the editor.
`Escape` aborts the running agent and restores any queued messages to the editor.
Starts an ephemeral side chat with its own transcript, without interrupting the main thread. Unavailable inside another side chat or during review mode.
Prefix input with `!` to run a shell command directly; the command and its output are added to the conversation and Claude responds automatically.
Output stays in the session; `Esc` leaves shell mode.
`/background [prompt]` detaches the session to keep running with no terminal attached; monitor it later with `claude agents`.
Spawns a completely separate agent session with its own history — it does not see your current conversation's context, though it inherits your model, provider, and toolsets.
Alias: `/sb`. A companion `/battery [on|off|status]` adds a color-coded battery readout to the status bar (off by default; no-op without a battery).
Opens your keyboard shortcuts file for editing; shortcuts vary by platform and terminal.
`/tui [default|fullscreen]` switches the renderer and relaunches with your conversation intact; fullscreen avoids flicker.
`/settings` opens Pi's settings UI, where you can switch the terminal interface between regular and fullscreen mode.
Renders flat text without borders or animations for screen readers; forces the classic renderer, overriding the `tui` setting.
Caps tool-calling iterations within a single turn (default: 500), not the number of prompts you send. Configurable via `agent.max_turns`.
`Ctrl+J` works in any terminal with no setup; `Shift+Enter` is native in some terminals but needs setup in others.
Opens the editor set by `$VISUAL` (or `$EDITOR` if unset); save and close returns the text to the composer before sending.
Enter with `/shell [command]` (aliases `/sh`, `/run`); exit with Escape, Backspace on empty input, or Ctrl+C. Long-running or interactive processes aren't supported.
Paste multiline text, like code blocks or logs, directly as a single block instead of submitting it line by line.
Large pastes collapse to a compact `[Pasted text #N]` reference in the input; recalling that prompt later resends the full pasted content.
Opens your prompt or response in your default text editor for editing; `Ctrl+X Ctrl+E` is the standard readline binding.
Use the editor newline binding to add a line without sending.
Multiline paste is integrated into one composer draft.
Since v0.6.0, large pastes show a short placeholder until submission.
Since v0.31.0, `Ctrl+C` clears a nonempty draft.
Multiline paste enters the prompt composer as one paste; longer text can appear as a compact placeholder until sent.
Since v1.0.26, pasted text of at least three lines or more than 150 characters can appear as a compact line-count marker. The full text is sent.
`Shift+Enter` inserts a newline while typing; use `Ctrl+Enter` instead on Windows Terminal.
Pasted multiline text is inserted together in the editor.
Large pastes appear as a compact marker; the full text is kept for submission.
`ctrl+c` (keybinding `app.clear`) clears the unsent prompt on its first press; a second press exits Pi.
Opens the current input in `$EDITOR` (`Ctrl+G` or `Ctrl+X Ctrl+E`). Saving and quitting sends the edited text immediately as your next prompt, rather than returning a draft.
Config-only: set `vim_mode: true` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, read at startup (CLI only, not messaging platforms).
`Ctrl+S` stashes your current draft and clears the composer; press it again on an empty composer to restore it. Stash also keeps attachments and multiline formatting.
Loads the most recent conversation in the current directory. Interactive use skips `-p`/SDK and `/loop`-first sessions.
Pass a session ID or name. A bare `--resume` opens the picker.
`-p` runs without the interactive UI; continuation can include earlier print-mode sessions.
Removes a background session from the list while keeping its local transcript resumable.
In agent view, `/resume` opens a picker of past sessions, including ones removed from the list; selecting one resumes it as a background session and it rejoins the active list.
Pass an absolute `.jsonl` transcript path to `--resume`.
Choose a previous point and rewind the conversation; the menu also offers code restoration or summarization.
The rewind menu can restore code. Symlinked and hard-linked tracked paths may be skipped.
`/resume` opens a picker for locally saved sessions.
`/fork` creates a new chat from the current one and leaves the original transcript intact.
With an empty composer, press `Esc` twice to edit the previous user message and fork from there.
Since v0.148.0, `/export` saves the complete TUI conversation as Markdown to a new file or clipboard.
Since v0.24.0, the TUI can rewind the conversation to an earlier prompt; use `Esc` to browse and `Enter` to select.
`agent ls` lists chats across workspaces by default, with a This-workspace toggle. `/resume` opens recent chats inside a session.
Pass the chat ID as `--resume [chatId]`; `--resume=-1` resumes the latest session.
Use `/rewind` (also `/undo` or `/restore`) to select an earlier turn and fully restore its files and conversation; choose conversation-only restore when files should remain unchanged.
`--continue` or `-c` resumes the latest CLI session; `--resume latest` uses the same lookup, which can be scoped to a workspace with `--in`.
In the classic CLI, `/sessions` opens a searchable picker of past sessions; bare `/resume` lists this chat's named sessions.
Since v2026.9.11, `hermes -z --resume` continues a saved session in one-shot mode.
`/branch` branches the current session in place in the CLI; it is refused while a turn is running.
`hermes sessions archive` soft-hides sessions matching prune-style filters (e.g. `--older-than`) without deleting them; requires at least one filter.
Since v2026.7.20, `hermes sessions export --format md` writes readable Markdown transcripts.
`hermes sessions export <output> [--session-id ID]` writes sessions to JSONL, a portable machine-readable format.
`hermes sessions import <path>` loads a Claude Code or Codex CLI session JSONL file for continuation.
`hermes sessions import` brings a Claude Code or Codex CLI conversation into Hermes and allows resuming it.
Since v2026.6.5, `/undo [N]` backs up conversation turns and prefills the last message for editing.
`/rollback <N>` (opt-in via `--checkpoints` or config) restores tracked files from a checkpoint and undoes the last conversation turn together; `--all` also overwrites hand-edits.
Use with `opencode run`, `opencode attach`, or TUI start to continue the last session.
Pass a session ID with `--session` or `-s` on `opencode run`, `opencode attach`, or TUI start.
`opencode run --continue` resumes the last session; `opencode run --session <id>` targets a specific session.
Through the server API, for example `opencode api session.fork`; omit `before` to copy the whole conversation.
Unbound by default; bind `session.fork` in `cli.json`.
`/undo` steps the conversation back to your prior message (and reverts the file changes made since); can be run repeatedly to undo multiple turns.
Startup flags (`-c` is the short form); continue the most recent session without a picker — `pi -r` opens the interactive session picker instead.
`--session <path|id>` selects a session file or partial session ID.
Since v0.22.5, `--session <path|id>` can resume a selected session in a one-shot `--print` run.
`/clone` copies the active conversation branch into a separate session file.
`/tree` moves to an earlier conversation point within the same session file; it does not restore files.
Requires a code-intelligence plugin for the language; inactive in cloud sessions.
Requires a code-intelligence plugin for the language; inactive in cloud sessions.
The experimental LSP tool can get type information at a position via a language server, once you install a code-intelligence plugin for your language.
Requires a code-intelligence plugin for the language; inactive in cloud sessions.
Reports type errors and warnings after edits when a language-server plugin is installed; inactive in cloud sessions.
`/plan` switches modes directly; `Shift+Tab` cycles through Agent, Plan, and Ask.
Plan mode (`/plan`, `--mode=plan`, Shift+Tab) is documented as read-only behavior, distinct from full-tool-access Agent mode.
Over ACP, `cursor/create_plan` is a blocking method: the agent submits its plan and waits for the client to approve or reject before continuing.
In ACP, the agent sends `cursor/update_todos` to add items to the client todo list; it is not a shell command.
Deletes a saved session by ID or name, including its transcript. `--force` skips confirmation only when the session is specified by UUID.
`hermes backup` creates a ZIP; `hermes import` restores it into Hermes home, overwriting existing files. Stop the gateway before importing.
`hermes sessions` includes deleting sessions; CLI sessions are stored in a local SQLite database.
Typing `/` opens a filterable popup of slash commands; queued slash commands still get completion before they run.
`Tab` completes a selected slash command from the popup.
Since v0.24.0, `Esc` or `Ctrl+C` can interrupt an active turn.
Since v0.98.0, `Enter` steers running work; `Tab` queues a follow-up.
Press `Tab` mid-turn to queue a follow-up prompt, slash command, or shell command that applies once the current turn finishes.
`Shift+Left` returns the last queued message to the composer for editing.
Since v0.25.0, interruption returns queued messages to the composer.
Runs under the current approval and sandbox settings.
Command output appears incrementally in the active tool preview.
/status prints a summary; /statusline can show model and context stats in the footer.
Bindings persist in config.toml; context-specific bindings override global ones.
`tui.alternate_screen` (auto/always/never) or the `--no-alt-screen` flag toggles the TUI's fullscreen alternate-screen buffer versus regular inline scrollback.
Since v2026.3.12, Up/Down recalls past prompts into the TUI input.
`Ctrl+C` interrupts the running agent; pressing it twice within 2 seconds force-exits.
`/steer <prompt>` (or `display.busy_input_mode: steer`) queues guidance that lands after the current tool call finishes, without interrupting the turn.
Up/Down selects a queued TUI prompt and loads it into input for editing.
On Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Matrix, `/branch` opens a sibling thread while the original chat stays on its session; `--here` branches in place. The CLI always branches in place.
`!` runs a direct shell command. `quick_commands` can expose configured exec commands as slash commands.
Toggle between the classic compact CLI and the fullscreen TUI with `hermes --tui` / `hermes --cli` (or `HERMES_TUI=1`), or set `display.interface: tui|cli` in config as the default.
Type `/` to open the command menu, then type letters to filter it. In fullscreen mode, press `Esc`, `i`, `/` to open the menu.
`Tab` accepts partial-path suggestions in `/cd` (v2.1.206+) and `/add-dir`.
Prompt history must be saved; `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1` keeps a session out of up-arrow history.
In fullscreen mode, `/` opens reverse history search; use `Esc`, `i`, `/` for the command menu.
Typing a message and pressing Enter while Claude works queues it in; once running tool calls finish, Claude receives it within the same turn, redirecting the turn without stopping it.
`Esc` stops the current turn mid-response or mid-tool-call, keeping work done so far, so you can immediately send a new instruction.
Typing a message and pressing Enter while Claude works queues it above the input box until it is sent, applying once the current step finishes.
Messages queued during a turn are sent automatically, in the order typed, once the agent finishes everything in that turn.
Pressing `Up` from the first input line pulls queued messages/commands back into the input box, one per line, for editing.
Pressing `Esc` to interrupt a running turn preserves anything already queued, which Claude Code then sends right away instead of discarding it.
`/btw [question]` keeps the side exchange out of the main conversation.
`/fork [prompt]` copies the current conversation into a new background session. `claude --bg` starts a new background session from the shell.
Since v2.1.259 or earlier, running shell commands show a live output preview.
Use `/status` for the model and `/context` for context usage; a custom status line can show `context_window.remaining_percentage`.
Set `background: true` in a subagent definition, or use `context: fork` in skill frontmatter; forked skills run in the background by default.
Since v2.1.217, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` overrides the default cap of 20 concurrent subagents.
Set `maxTurns` in a subagent definition. At the limit, Claude Code returns partial output and can resume the subagent.
The background panel below the prompt lists the main session and each running fork/subagent; press Enter on a row to open its transcript and steer it, Esc to return focus to the main session.
In agent teams, the lead creates tasks with TaskCreate into a shared task list that teammates claim and work through; tasks can depend on other tasks.
Subagent workflows are enabled by default in current Codex releases.
The built-in `explorer` role is for read-heavy codebase exploration; a custom agent with the same name takes precedence.
Since v0.107.0, `spawn_agent` lets a child agent work in the background while the parent continues other work.
Set `agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session` in config.toml. `agents.max_threads` remains a legacy alias.
`agents.max_depth` limits V1 agent thread nesting; V2 ignores this setting.
Use `/agent` (alias `/subagents`) to inspect or continue a spawned agent's thread in the interactive session.
Since v0.156.0, agent message-board tools let agents in one collaboration post and read shared channels.
Subagents run locally with their own context and tokens in interactive and headless CLI sessions.
Requires an ACP client over stdio; the agent waits for the client's JSON-RPC response.
Since v0.24.0, the installable `subagent` example delegates to isolated Pi processes.
Since v0.24.0, the optional `subagent` example includes a scout for codebase reconnaissance.
Since v0.24.0, the optional `subagent` example accepts a per-agent `tools` list in Markdown frontmatter.
Since v0.24.0, the optional `subagent` example caps parallel execution at four concurrent children.
`/bg <prompt>` starts an isolated agent session; the foreground session stays interactive, and results appear in a panel.
The `/agents` (alias `/tasks`, Ctrl+T) overlay shows a live subagent tree; select a child for its live transcript, steer it (`e`), or stop it, then return to the main session.
The `kanban` toolset coordinates agents through a shared board and dispatcher. It must be enabled explicitly; `all/*` does not enable it.
Since v2026.5.28, `hermes kanban swarm` creates parallel worker cards with gated verification; Kanban tasks can use separate worktrees.
Set `permissions` in the subagent definition; the child uses its own rules.
Set `steps` on a subagent to limit its agentic iterations. At the limit, it is prompted to summarize remaining work.
Since v0.44.0, the `notify.ts` extension example sends a desktop terminal notification when Pi finishes and waits for input.
Set `notify` to an external notifier command to receive an alert after a turn completes; the TUI also supports terminal desktop notifications.
Enable `notifications` in CLI config for terminal alerts when the agent finishes or needs input.
Enable `attention` in `tui.json`; desktop notifications appear when the terminal is blurred. Attention is off by default.
Set `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` to a percentage from 1 to 100 of the auto-compact window.
Manages Routines on claude.ai. Requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan; organization policy can remove the tool.
The anthropics/claude-code-action GitHub Action runs on a `schedule: cron` workflow trigger in automation mode with a `prompt` input; GitHub only runs scheduled workflows from the default branch.
An MCP server can declare the channel capability so webhook events push directly into a running session, opted in per session with `--channels`.

Channels (Telegram, Discord, iMessage) act as a two-way chat bridge into a running session; keep it durable by running Claude Code as a background process or persistent terminal so events keep arriving.

Installing the official Telegram channel plugin and starting Claude Code with `--channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official` lets you message Claude from Telegram after pairing with `/telegram:access pair`.
`/loop [interval] <prompt>` reruns on a fixed or self-paced cadence in the live session; distinct from `/cron` (detached) and `/goal` (judge-driven, not timer-based).
`/heartbeat every <interval> <prompt>` schedules a recurring prompt in the current session while idle. One heartbeat is allowed per session.
`/heartbeat status` shows the current session heartbeat, its interval, and time to next fire.
`/heartbeat clear` removes the recurring prompt scheduled in the current session.
Setting `bell_on_complete: true` (or `bell_on_prompt`) also emits an OSC 9 desktop notification on terminals that support it (Ghostty, iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm); Warp gets its own OSC 777 event.
Configure the `ntfy` messaging platform (a phone push-notification channel); replies and cron deliveries land as phone push notifications, including outgoing-only alert setups.
Codex reads `AGENTS.md` for project guidance. `project_doc_max_bytes` caps discovered instruction text.
Set `developer_instructions` in config.toml to add guidance as a developer message.
`model_instructions_file` points to a file that overrides built-in model instructions; the source strongly discourages this setting.
Project rules live in `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`; the CLI also reads root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
Use `globs` frontmatter in `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` to apply a project rule to matching files.
Write `@filename.ext` inside a rule body to pull that file's contents into the rule's context.
`/context` breaks down what's consuming the context window by category.
Project files are discovered from the working directory with priority and size caps; a lower-priority file may be shadowed or truncated.
`/context` (alias `/ctx`) shows a glyph grid plus a per-category token breakdown (system prompt, tools, rules, skills, MCP, memory, conversation); `/context all` adds per-skill/per-toolset costs.
Add a focus topic to `/compress` to steer what its summary preserves.
Set `compression.threshold` in config.yaml (default 0.50 = compress at 50% of the context limit) to change when auto-compaction fires.
`/compress here [N]` manually summarizes history while keeping the most recent N exchanges verbatim (default 2). Automatic compression instead preserves a fixed last 20 turns.
Put an `AGENTS.md` in a subdirectory; it applies when the agent works there.
Set `instructions` to include additional instruction files alongside the default model system prompt; a custom agent prompt can replace that default prompt.
Set per agent; project instructions, skills and references are still added.
A percentage of each model’s window, for example `"buffer": "20%"`.
Save a Markdown file directly in `~/.codex/prompts/`. New or edited prompts load after a restart or new chat.
Codex lists skill names and descriptions first, then reads the full `SKILL.md` when it uses a skill.
Use a `$` mention to name a skill directly, or `/skills` to choose one for the next request.
Since v0.97.0, changed skill files are picked up without restarting.
Register a server with `codex mcp add`; its tools become available through MCP. Stdio servers use a local command, and HTTP servers use a URL.
Add a Markdown file under `~/.codex/prompts/` and invoke it from the slash command menu as `/prompts:<name>`; requires a session restart to pick up new files.
Add a local marketplace root with `codex plugin marketplace add`, then install its plugin with `codex plugin add`. Bundled skills and tools apply in a new session.
A Markdown file in `.claude/commands/` creates a reusable named command; this legacy format still works.
A skill's body (the `SKILL.md` instructions beyond its short description) loads into context only when the skill is invoked, either automatically or via `/skill-name`.
Connect a server that provides the tool; the tool is then available through MCP.
A Markdown file in `.claude/commands/` becomes a `/<name>` command; custom commands are now merged with skills.
`--plugin-dir` loads local plugin directories or `.zip` archives for the current session only.
Mods are plugins written in JavaScript or TypeScript. A `ui.render` hook draws a pane, a band above the prompt, buttons and text fields. Added in v2.1.287.
A mod's `ui.render` hook can change or replace how a tool call and its result are drawn, at the `ToolUse`, `ToolResult` and `ToolGroup` render sites.
Set `disable-model-invocation: true` in a `SKILL.md` skill to make it available only through `/skill-name`, rather than auto-applying it.
Cursor auto-discovers `SKILL.md` files and loads their extra resources only when a task needs them, keeping unused skills out of context.
Running `/add-dir` mid-session refreshes discovered skills and custom commands right away; a full restart is only needed for fully automatic rediscovery.
Configure an MCP server in `mcp.json`; tool use is subject to approval and run mode.
Add command files as a plugin `commands` component; plugin reload refreshes slash commands.
`--plugin-dir <path>` loads a local plugin for a run; `enabled_plugins` in `~/.cursor/settings.json` loads local folders.
The `template` defines the prompt for a custom TUI command.
Since v1.1.48, skills can be invoked as slash commands in the TUI. `/skills` opens a picker that inserts the selected skill command.
Markdown filenames become command names. Custom commands can override built-in commands with the same name.
`-e`/`--extension` loads code for one run; `pi install <source>` persists a package. Project-local extensions in `.pi/extensions/` load after project trust.
Returns numbered lines; long reads are paginated and may be truncated around 100K characters.
Overwrites the whole file. An existing file needs a current full read before writing.
Targeted find-and-replace uses fuzzy matching when whitespace or indentation differs.
`patch` with `mode=patch` applies one structured V4A patch across files.
Finds files by name using a ripgrep-backed tool.
Searches file contents with a ripgrep-backed tool.
`/learn` turns supplied material into a reusable `SKILL.md`; installed skills are exposed as dynamic slash commands in CLI sessions.
Built-in commands take precedence on name collisions; use `/skill <name>` for the skill.
`/reload-skills` (alias `/reload_skills`) re-scans `~/.hermes/skills/` mid-session for newly installed or removed skills.
Custom tools load through a plugin; add the plugin's name to `plugins.enabled`.
Define `quick_commands` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`; exec commands run without invoking the model.
User plugins need `plugins.enabled`; project plugins also need `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=true` before startup.
The `apply_patch` tool can create a complete new file with `*** Add File:` and added content lines.
Agent reads file content through tool calls; file access is subject to read permissions and hooks.
Shows in `--output-format stream-json` as a `writeToolCall` event.
Agent has a Search files and folders tool that finds files by name, separate from its keyword/pattern content search.
Built-in Agent search runs automatically; its index is local.
Supports specific line ranges. Default permissions deny `.env` and `.env.*`, while allowing `.env.example`.
Creates files and overwrites existing ones; controlled by the `edit` permission.
Modifies existing files through exact string replacements.
Returns matching paths sorted by modification time.
Supports regular expressions and file-pattern filtering.
`read` is in the default tool set.
The built-in `write` tool creates a new file or overwrites an existing one completely.
The built-in `edit` tool swaps out an exact text match in a file.
The built-in `find` tool locates files by matching their path against glob patterns.
`grep` is built in but is outside the default enabled set; enable it with `--tools`.

A `PreCompact` hook can cancel compaction (exit code 2 or `{"decision":"block"}`); it cannot supply a replacement summary — Claude Code discards the hook's `systemMessage`/`continue` fields on this event.
The source matcher distinguishes startup, resume, clear, and compact.
`SessionEnd` runs synchronously; its default timeout is 1 second and its maximum is 3 seconds.
Runs before a prompt is sent; it can add developer context or block the prompt.
Can deny or rewrite supported local tool calls before execution; some specialized tool paths opt out.
Runs after supported local tools produce output, including Bash nonzero exits; it cannot undo side effects.
Runs only when Codex is about to ask for approval; a hook can allow, deny, or decline to decide.
Its matcher can distinguish manual from automatic compaction.
In a `PreCompact` hook, `continue: false` stops Codex before chat compaction runs.
Can add developer context to the subagent; `continue: false` does not prevent launch.
A block decision with a reason can request continuation of the subagent flow.
Configure `sessionStart` hooks in `.cursor/hooks.json` or `~/.cursor/hooks.json`; cloud agents run only the project-level command-based subset.
Configure `sessionEnd` in `.cursor/hooks.json` or `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, or through a plugin.
`beforeSubmitPrompt` can validate and block a prompt before submission.
`preToolUse` covers tool calls generally; the other hooks target shell commands, MCP tools, and file reads. Configure hooks in `hooks.json`.
`postToolUse` runs after a tool call finishes.
Configure a `postToolUseFailure` hook in `hooks.json` to run custom logic specifically when a tool call fails, times out, or is denied.
An ACP client must answer `session/request_permission` for tool approvals; unanswered requests can block execution.
A `subagentStart` hook in `hooks.json` fires before a subagent is spawned and can allow or deny its creation.
A `subagentStop` hook in `hooks.json` fires when a subagent finishes, errors, or is aborted, and can trigger a follow-up message.
`on_session_start` only fires for a brand-new session, not when continuing or resuming an existing one — there is no separate resume event.
An observer plugin hook; its return value is ignored.
`pre_llm_call` fires once per turn before the model call and can inject or modify context alongside the user's message, filling the same role as a UserPromptSubmit hook.
Set `SECURITY_GUIDANCE_BLOCK=1` to have `security-guidance` refuse matching `write_file` and `patch` writes; its default is warn mode.
Plugin hooks must be allowlisted. `post_tool_call` runs after every tool invocation, not only successful ones.
Plugins register `subagent_start` via `ctx.register_hook("subagent_start", callback)`, one of the 27 lifecycle events in `hermes_cli.plugins.VALID_HOOKS`.
Plugins register `subagent_stop` via `ctx.register_hook("subagent_stop", callback)`, fired when a delegated subagent finishes.
Since v1.0.50, plugins can use `chat.message` to inspect or change message parts before the submitted message is saved for the agent.
Implement `tool.execute.before` in a plugin. It can change tool arguments or block a call by throwing.
Implement `tool.execute.after` in a plugin; it receives tool input and output after execution.
One `execute.after` hook; check `event.status === "error"` for failures.
A server plugin hook.
This experimental plugin hook runs before the LLM writes the compaction summary. It can add context or replace the summary prompt.
A server plugin hook that supplies its own summary.
Extension event; fires on startup, reload, new session, resume, and fork.
Extension event before session teardown, including quit, reload, new, resume, and fork.
The extension `input` event fires with the submitted text before the agent processes it, and a handler can transform or block it.
The extension `tool_result` event fires after any tool call completes and can inspect or modify the result (check `isError` for success).
Since v0.31.0, handle `tool_result` and check `isError` to run logic when a tool fails.
Extension event `session_before_compact` fires before history is condensed, with the messages to summarize, the previous summary and reason manual/threshold/overflow; received by loaded extensions.
Slash autocomplete includes user-invocable skills; skills marked `user-invocable: false` are hidden.
Press up-arrow in the input box to recall previously typed prompts from the current conversation's history.
`Ctrl+C` ends the running turn; transport interruptions now retry automatically instead.
Type a message and press Enter while the agent is working to steer the current turn at a safe boundary, without stopping it.
Press Enter twice on an empty prompt to stop the current turn and immediately send a new queued message.
Type a follow-up prompt while the agent is still working; it queues and submits once the current turn finishes.
`/btw` (alias `/side`) opens a read-only side question in an overlay; it never touches the main conversation history.
Since April 2026, `Ctrl+Z` sends the CLI to the background and returns control to the terminal.
Slash commands appear in the prompt autocomplete as you type; choosing one inserts its command name.
Tab is the default keybind (`prompt.autocomplete.complete`) to accept the current autocomplete suggestion in the input box.
`Enter` steers the running turn; `Ctrl+X` then `Enter` queues the prompt instead.
Prompts entered while an ordinary turn runs wait in a queue and can be managed before their turn begins.
`End` follows new output while the command runs.
The TUI prompt shows the selected model and current context usage as a token count and percentage.
Set `keybinds` in `tui.json`; only changed shortcuts need entries. The old `opencode.json` key is deprecated.
Typing `/` opens a searchable, filterable list of available slash commands as you type.
`Tab` completes paths in the editor.
The Up arrow (keybinding `tui.editor.historyPrevious`) pulls the previous submitted prompt back into the editor.
Since v0.25.0, a message sent during tool execution stops the remaining tool batch and redirects the agent after the current tool.
Since v0.32.0, send steering messages with Enter or queue follow-ups with Alt+Enter; settings choose how many messages to deliver at a time.
`!command` sends output to the model; `!!command` keeps output out of the model context.
Since v0.25.3, Ctrl+Z suspends Pi and frees the terminal; use `fg` to resume. Native Windows does not support it.
The interactive TUI shows tool calls and results as they happen, and JSON/RPC mode emits `tool_execution_update` events carrying live `partialResult` output while a tool runs.
The footer continuously shows the current model and context usage.
Create `<agent-dir>/keybindings.json` assigning named actions (e.g. `app.session.new`) to one or more keys, then `/reload`; `/hotkeys` shows the active shortcuts.
Print mode runs the prompt without opening the interactive UI and exits after returning the response.
`--max-turns` (print mode only) caps the agentic turns Claude Code takes while working through one prompt and exits with an error at the limit; subagents have their own `maxTurns` frontmatter field.
Use `codex exec --output-schema <file>` to get the final response validated against a JSON Schema, or `--json` for a full newline-delimited JSON event stream.
`codex app-server` is experimental. Stdio is the default transport; `--stdio` selects it explicitly.
Embed via `@openai/codex-sdk` (TypeScript, Node 18+) or `openai-codex` (Python 3.10+); both start/resume threads against the local Codex app-server.
`codex remote-control` runs an experimental daemon that the ChatGPT mobile/desktop Remote app pairs with via `codex remote-control pair`, so a phone or another device can steer the session.
Use `-p` or `--print` for a scripted run. Applying file changes can require `--force`; an untrusted workspace can require `--trust` or `--force`.
Use `--output-format json` with print mode. On failure, the process may write an error to stderr without a JSON result.
Use `--output-format stream-json` with print mode. Add `--stream-partial-output` for incremental text deltas.
The hidden `agent acp` command serves JSON-RPC 2.0 to custom clients over stdin/stdout, with one message per line.
`cursor-sdk-bridge` runs a local HTTP/1.1 server exposing the agent over Connect/protobuf RPCs (or plain POSTs), for languages without a first-party SDK.
The official `@cursor/sdk` (TypeScript) and Python SDK embed the same agent loop used by the IDE, CLI and web app directly into your own application code.
`hermes -z` prints only the final response. On a TTY, `hermes chat -q` needs `--oneshot` or `-Q` to answer and exit.
Use `--format stream-json` with `-q` or `--query`; it emits JSONL and implies quiet mode.
`--max-turns <N>` caps tool-calling iterations per turn for a run (default 500, or `agent.max_turns` in config).
`hermes acp` starts an ACP stdio server (bidirectional RPC) for editor integration; install the acp extra first.
Set `API_SERVER_ENABLED=true` and `API_SERVER_KEY`, then run `hermes gateway`; the local HTTP server uses bearer authentication.
Hermes Desktop connects to the dashboard's `/api/ws` through a signed-in `Remote URL`. A non-loopback dashboard bind requires authentication.
Install the `acp` extra before starting the ACP stdio server; older installs may need `hermes update` for the `hermes-acp` launcher.
Official Python library guide: `from run_agent import AIAgent`, then `agent.chat(...)` or `run_conversation()` to embed the full agent loop in your own code.
`hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0` binds the browser dashboard non-locally; its Chat tab drives the local session over PTY/WebSocket from any browser, phone included, behind a required auth provider.
Use with `opencode run`; JSON output contains raw events as the run progresses.
Agent config `steps` (e.g. `"steps": 5`) caps agentic tool-call iterations before the agent is forced to respond with text only; unset means it iterates until the model or user stops it.
`opencode acp` starts an ACP server speaking newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio for editor integrations.
Pairing links expire after 5 minutes and work once; `--remote` exposes the server through OpenTunnel.
Prints the response and exits; piped stdin is merged into the initial prompt. Non-interactive project trust settings apply.
`--mode json` runs one-shot and writes JSONL events to stdout; the `message_end` event carries the authoritative final assistant message for scripts to parse.
Emits events as JSON lines on stdout for non-interactive integrations.
HTTP is the recommended remote transport. JSON entries require an explicit `type`; a URL alone is not enough.
Use `disable` from `/mcp` to turn off a server connection; `enable` turns it back on.
Run `/mcp` without arguments to open the server list; in `-p` mode it prints a status summary on v2.1.205+.
Put `mcp__<server>__<tool>` in a deny or ask permission rule to restrict one tool. Allow rules preapprove access instead.
Works with Streamable HTTP servers that support OAuth; it does not authenticate stdio servers.
Use `/mcp` in an interactive session to inspect available MCP servers and tools; `/mcp verbose` adds server diagnostics.
`/mcp` lists the MCP tools available in the session; `/mcp verbose` adds detailed per-server diagnostics.
Since v0.143.0, MCP tools are found through `tool_search` and exposed when needed.
The app-server JSON-RPC method `mcpServerStatus/list` returns each MCP server's tools, resources and auth status (`detail: "full"` includes resources).
The app-server JSON-RPC method `mcpServer/resource/read` reads a single MCP resource from a connected server.
Configure the local server command in project or user `mcp.json`; it must be on PATH or use a full path.
Configure the HTTP endpoint in `mcp.json`; server authentication may require OAuth.
Put the tool token in `permissions.deny` in global or project CLI configuration; wildcards can match servers or tools.
Configure a `mcp_servers` entry with `command` and optional `args` and `env`; there is no `stdio` key.
Set `url` to the remote endpoint. Streamable HTTP is the default; `transport: sse` selects SSE.
Use `hermes mcp login <server>` from a fresh terminal; `--flow device` selects device-code login.
Set `enabled: false` under an entry in `mcp_servers:` in config.yaml to disable a server while keeping its configuration.
`hermes mcp list` lists configured servers; `hermes mcp test <name>` checks a server's connection status.
Since v2026.6.5, MCP and plugin tools can be found with `tool_search`, loaded with `tool_describe`, and invoked with `tool_call`.
Use original MCP tool names in `include` and `exclude`, including any hyphens or dots.
Hermes registers a per-server `mcp_<server>_list_resources` utility tool when the MCP session supports resource operations.
Hermes registers a per-server `read_resource` utility tool to pull a specific resource by URI when the server supports it.
Hermes registers per-server `get_prompt`/`list_prompts` utility tools (e.g. `mcp_github_get_prompt`) so the agent can run a server-supplied prompt.
Servers go under `mcp.servers`; V2 no longer puts server names directly under `mcp`.
OAuth authorization opens a browser; tokens are stored in `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json`.
Use `permission` rules matching MCP tool names, with `deny` or `ask` for selected tools.
Since v1.17.10, `list_mcp_resources` lists resources from a connected server or all connected servers.
Since v1.17.10, `read_mcp_resource` reads a server resource by its URI.
Built into Pi since 0.99.0. `pi mcp add <name> -- <command>` writes `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`; add `-l` for the project's `.pi/mcp.json`, read only in trusted projects.
Built into Pi since 0.99.0. The legacy SSE transport is not supported.
Over SSH, paste the redirected URL into the sign-in screen. Credentials are kept per server.
Disable in `/mcp` or set `enabled: false`. In a trusted project, `/mcp` can disable a user-level server for that project only.
The `mcp({ search })` proxy tool returns a matching tool's name, description, and parameter schema without connecting first.
Set a server's `exposure` to `deferred`. The default, `codemode`, reaches tools from codemode scripts instead.
Set a tool, or a `*` pattern, to `hidden` in `toolExposure`. `--tools` and `--exclude-tools` accept `mcp__<server>__*` patterns for one run.
Built-in MCP support (since 0.99.0). The tools appear when a connected server offers resources.
Text reaches the model as text and images as images; other binary resources are saved to temporary files.
Image files can be dragged or pasted into the terminal prompt.
`Ctrl+V`/`Cmd+V` (iTerm2) or `Alt+V` (Windows/WSL) pastes a clipboard image into the prompt as an `[Image #N]` chip you can reference positionally.
Since v0.156.0, voice conversations are enabled by default in the TUI. Press F8 to toggle; use `/voice settings` to choose a voice.
`--image <path>` attaches a local image to one `hermes query`/`-q` invocation.
Use `/paste` when an image-only clipboard or terminal paste does not trigger attachment. Shortcut behavior depends on terminal and clipboard access.
`Ctrl+B` starts push-to-talk recording; `voice.record_key` can change the key. Recording stops after silence.
`--image` attaches image files in interactive and print sessions.
Paste a clipboard image into the interactive prompt with `Ctrl+V`; analysis requires a vision-capable model.
Image generation depends on model and client support. It creates images from text descriptions or reference images and saves them to the project `assets/` folder by default.
Since v1.0.186, `Ctrl+V` pastes a clipboard image into the TUI prompt, including on Windows.
Experimental; appears while a connected provider has an image model.
Paste with `Ctrl+V` (`Alt+V` on Windows); the selected provider and model must accept images.

Requires the `pi-web-access` extension package; it analyzes a YouTube URL or local video file for transcripts, visual descriptions, and timestamped frames (optional ffmpeg/yt-dlp for frame extraction).
Generation runs from a codemode script and needs an image model, such as one on OpenRouter. Since v1.0.0; images are also saved to temp files since v1.0.3.

Auto memory records a `user` note kind (your role, expertise, working preferences) as its own topic file, separate from `project`, `feedback`, and `reference` notes about the work, indexed together in `MEMORY.md`.
`/memory` views auto memory entries.
Use `/memory` to edit `CLAUDE.md` files; these persistent instruction files load in later sessions.
Since v0.135.0, the dedicated `memories.read` tool reads a saved Codex memory file by relative path.
Since v0.135.0, `memories.add_ad_hoc_note` saves a note when you explicitly ask Codex to remember, forget, or update something.
Since v0.129.0, `memories.search` searches saved memory files; it supports multiple queries and optional normalized matching.
Requires an initialized, running OpenViking server and provider setup.
External memory-provider plugins (Hindsight, Supermemory, Memori Cloud) expose explicit lookup tools like `hindsight_recall` / `supermemory_search` / `memori_recall` to read saved memory on demand.
The built-in `memory` tool lets the model save a note to persistent memory (subject to `memory.write_approval`).
Set up the Honcho provider with `hermes memory setup`; it requires `honcho-ai` plus an API key or self-hosted instance. Use `honcho_search` for semantic search.
The Hindsight memory provider exposes separate `auto_recall` (use existing memory) and `auto_retain` (write new memory) config keys, so either can be toggled independently.

Requires the `pi-persistent-intelligence` extension; it auto-captures preference/observation candidates during work without a special command, but each candidate needs inbox review before becoming durable memory.

Requires the `pi-persistent-intelligence` extension; durable memory writes are patch-governed and go through inbox review before being applied (session-scoped L3 notes are freely writable without review).
Run `/model` without an argument to open the picker. Available choices depend on provider, account, plan, region, and organization policy.

An `availableModels` allowlist (managed/policy settings) restricts which models appear in the `/model` quick-switch picker; pair it with `enforceAvailableModels` to also constrain the picker's Default option.
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` routes through a proxy or gateway. Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform have separate provider settings and interactive setup wizards.
`/model` opens a popup to change the active model during a session.
`/model` opens a popup to choose the active model in the TUI; `codex debug models` prints the raw model catalog (optionally `--bundled` only) from the terminal.
A custom `model_catalog_json` can set each model’s `visibility` to `list` or `hide`, controlling which models appear in the `/model` picker.
`/model` can change effort in a session. `model_reasoning_effort` sets it in config for supported Responses API models; available levels depend on the model.
`/model` opens the picker; `/composer` and `/opus` jump to a family and remember its last choice. Family shortcuts can be disabled in `/config`.
`/model [filter]` opens the picker; availability depends on the account, plan, and team settings.
Model IDs accept bracketed options, e.g. `claude-opus-5[effort=high]`, to set reasoning effort explicitly per model/subagent.
Amazon Bedrock with your own credentials; other custom endpoints are not described.
Switches among configured providers and models. Changing models mid-conversation resets the prompt cache.
Run `/model` with no arguments to browse configured provider-model options; it cannot add providers, and switching resets the prompt cache.
The picker offers a reasoning-effort step when the selected route supports it.
Configure an ordered chain with `hermes fallback` or `fallback_providers` in `config.yaml`; the primary is retried each turn.
Run `hermes model` outside a chat session and choose `Custom endpoint`; the choice is saved in `config.yaml`.
Connect a self-hosted Ollama or vLLM endpoint through the custom endpoint setup.
A plugin under `~/.hermes/plugins/model-providers/<name>/` calling `register_provider(ProviderProfile(...))` can add a new provider or override a bundled one of the same name.
The `/models` command (keybind `ctrl+x m`) lists and switches models mid-session; `--model`/`-m` sets it at launch.
Per-provider `blacklist`/`whitelist` model-ID arrays in opencode.json trim which models appear in the `/models` picker; combine both to narrow then exclude.
Choose a variant with `#`, for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5#high`, or cycle with `Ctrl+T`.
For aggregator providers (e.g. OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway), per-model `options.provider.order`/`only`/`zeroDataRetention` control which upstream providers the aggregator routes requests to.
`Ctrl+P` cycles through the models enabled for cycling.
`/model` opens the model picker; `Ctrl+L` also opens it.
Add providers and endpoints in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; set a provider's `baseUrl` for a proxy or custom endpoint.
Configure a local server in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; the model server runs separately.
Since v0.50.0, `openRouterRouting` configures upstream provider routing for custom OpenRouter models.
`/reload-plugins` may skip MCP tool changes to protect the prompt cache unless `--force` is used. `/reload-skills` re-scans skill and command directories.

Claude Code can run installed as an OS service hosting the background-session supervisor; `claude daemon status` inspects it and `claude daemon stop` (or `claude daemon stop --any` for an on-demand supervisor) stops it.
`DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` turns off anonymous usage-metrics reporting; `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0` omits the client-version/prompt-fingerprint attribution block from the system prompt.
Since v0.97.0, skill file changes update live; v0.154.0 also refreshes plugin tools, skills, and hooks in existing sessions after plugin changes.
For `codex exec`, `--ignore-user-config` skips `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`; authentication still uses `CODEX_HOME`.
`codex remote-control start`/`stop` (experimental) start and stop the local app-server daemon as a background service.
