`/usage` shows daily, weekly and cumulative token activity (requires Codex service account auth); `/status` shows current session token usage, model and approval policy.
Set `[analytics] enabled = false` in config.toml to turn off the anonymous usage/health metrics Codex otherwise sends by default, across the desktop app, CLI and IDE extension.
Reloading a plugin live-refreshes its slash commands, palette entries and MCP tool leases without restarting the CLI session.
`/usage` shows included-usage meters, on-demand spend against your limit, plan name and billing-cycle reset date for the current session/account.
Use `/reload-mcp` for MCP servers or `hermes bundles reload` to re-scan `~/.hermes/skill-bundles/`; no reload-all command is described.
`/usage` shows this session's token usage, cost breakdown, duration and, when supported, remaining provider quota/credits; `hermes usage` reports the same account-limits block without a session.
The dashboard's Analytics page (and `hermes insights`) aggregates token usage and cost by day, and by model with per-model session counts.
Since v2026.8.3, configure `monitoring.export.otlp` to send gateway health metrics, lifecycle traces and diagnostic logs to an OTLP endpoint. It excludes run and tool content.
Since v2026.7.20, add `--redact` to `hermes sessions export` to scrub API keys, tokens and credentials from exported content.
`opencode service restart` and `set`/`get` manage its settings.
Run `opencode stats` to see token usage and cost, with `--days`, `--tools`, `--models`, `--project` filters.
`/session` shows session tokens and cost; the footer also shows context use. Neither reports remaining provider account quota.
With no target, these commands review the current diff.
`/code-review [branch]` or `/ultrareview [branch]` reviews everything changed against that branch instead of the default base.
Since v2026.3.17, `/plan` makes the current turn planning-only and saves a plan; it does not start implementation.
`/plan [task]` inspects context and writes a markdown implementation plan under `.hermes/plans/` without executing or changing anything.
The `todo_list` tool manages a session's tracked task list, including nested subtasks via a `parent` field.
Kanban toolset tools `kanban_list` (orchestrator) and `kanban_show` (worker) list board tasks and show one task's title, description, comments and dependencies.
`/review [instructions]` then starts a reviewer subagent on the work just discussed.
Experimental and off by default in OpenCode 2.
The bundled `plan-mode/` example extension lets users toggle read-only planning with `/plan` or `Ctrl+Alt+P`; it must be loaded as an extension.
The bundled `plan-mode/` example asks what to do after a plan is formed. Choosing “Execute the plan (track progress)” exits planning and starts execution.
Use `-p` with a review prompt. `--tools read,grep,find,ls` restricts the run to read-only tools.
Repository-supplied allow rules and additional directories only take effect after you accept the workspace trust dialog for that folder.
Accepting workspace trust persists for the repository root or start directory; a session started in your home directory keeps trust only for that session.
Use `Read(path)` rules in permissions settings; they also affect Grep, Glob, and LSP access.
Use `Edit(path)` rules for path-scoped file changes, including Write. `Write(path)` rules are accepted but are not checked for file paths.
Bash permission patterns match command text; alternate shell spellings can evade a literal prefix pattern.
A matching deny rule wins across settings scopes and even in bypassPermissions mode.
The sandbox's `filesystem.allowWrite`/`allowRead`/`denyWrite`/`denyRead` settings scope which paths the built-in sandbox can read or write, beyond the default working directory and added directories.
Sandbox network settings limit domains reached by sandboxed commands; a new domain requires approval. Available on macOS, Linux, and WSL2.
Run Claude Code inside a Docker or dev container to isolate the whole process; this requires external container tooling.
`worktree.baseRef` selects the remote default branch (`fresh`) or current `HEAD` (`head`); it does not accept a branch name.
Project-level `.codex/config.toml`, hooks and rules load only once you trust that project folder.
Add `[projects."/path/to/project"] trust_level = "untrusted"` under `~/.codex/config.toml` to persist a stricter trust decision for that folder.
Set `apps.<id>.tools.<tool>.approval_mode` (`auto|prompt|writes|approve`) or the matching `mcp_servers.<id>.tools.<tool>` keys, and toggle `.enabled` to block a tool outright.
Beta permission profiles use path or scoped subpath entries in `permissions.<name>.filesystem`; `deny` blocks reads and writes.
Beta permission profiles use path or scoped subpath entries in `permissions.<name>.filesystem`; `write` permits modifications and `deny` blocks access.
For matching command rules, `forbidden` wins over `prompt` and `allow`. Execpolicy rules are experimental.
Set `approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"` with an interactive approval policy. Only requests that already need approval reach the reviewer.
Sandboxed commands use platform isolation: macOS Seatbelt, Linux Landlock/seccomp, or the native Windows sandbox.
Use the Codex secure devcontainer reference (`.devcontainer/devcontainer.secure.json`) to run the whole CLI inside a Docker-isolated Dev Container.
Since v0.154.0, `--worktree` starts an isolated checkout for a new or forked session.
A trust dialog gates unfamiliar workspaces; `--trust` skips it (headless mode, and interactive sessions since it also works there).
`--trust` saves the workspace trust decision. The parameters reference calls it headless only, while the July 2026 changelog also documents interactive use.
Set `permissions.allow`/`permissions.deny` tokens like `Shell()`, `Read()`, `Write()`, `Mcp()` in `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` or project `.cursor/cli.json`; deny wins over allow.
`Shell(commandBase)` matches the first command token; use command:args globs for finer control. Configure it in global or project CLI permissions.
Auto-review uses a classifier for remaining tool calls and can still ask you. Availability depends on team controls and classifier model access; it is not a security boundary.
Sandboxed commands use Seatbelt on macOS or Landlock and seccomp on Linux. If sandboxing is unavailable, Cursor asks for approval instead.
`sandbox.json` at `~/.cursor/sandbox.json` (global) or `<project>/.cursor/sandbox.json` (project, takes priority) sets extra readable/writable paths for the sandbox.
Set domain policy in `sandbox.json`; `sandbox.networkAccess` controls the sandbox network mode. Team policy takes precedence.

Project-local skills under `.hermes/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` are not auto-loaded from a cloned repo; run `hermes skills trust` once per repo before its skills (procedure code the agent follows) activate.
Trusting a project (`hermes skills trust`) persists the repo path in `skills.trusted_project_dirs`; `hermes skills untrust` revokes it.
Use `approvals.deny` glob rules to block terminal commands; `approvals.mode` is `smart`, `manual`, or `off`, and `command_allowlist` supplies exec-approval patterns.
`HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT` limits file-tool writes to a safe root; protected paths remain blocked. The terminal tool runs as the same OS user and can still modify those paths.
Set `approvals.deny` to block matching terminal commands, including in YOLO mode. This is command matching, not an OS sandbox.
Matching `approvals.deny` rules block terminal commands even when approval shortcuts or command allowlisting would permit them.
`approvals.mode: smart` uses an auxiliary model to assess dangerous commands and escalates uncertain cases.
Set `terminal.backend` to `docker`, `singularity`, or `modal` for container or remote sandbox execution. Backend setup is required.
`--worktree` or `-w` starts in a separate Git worktree; `/worktree new` creates one during an interactive session. Requires a Git repository.
The bash action is now `shell`.
Install the `pi-landstrip` extension. With sandboxing enabled, AI Bash uses OS isolation; enabled sandboxing fails closed if its native binary or platform is unusable.
Deletes the selected session and all its data.
Delete a saved session from the interactive session picker (`/resume` or `pi --resume`), which supports search, rename, and delete.
Only bash or zsh; other shells such as fish are not supported.
Also wraps hook, status line and stdio MCP server commands.
Use `--bg` with `--exec` for a PTY-backed shell job; `--bg` alone starts a background Claude session.
`/tasks` shows background work in the current session.
`/tasks` (alias `/bashes`) and `claude agents`/agent view show whether background commands and subagents have finished.
`TaskOutput` is deprecated; read the task's output file with `Read` instead.
The default `shell` tool is enabled by `features.shell_tool`; sandbox and approval settings govern command execution.
The `shell` argument selects the shell binary for agent command execution when that parameter is exposed.
Since v0.24.0, `exec_command` can return a `session_id` for a still-running shell command.
`/ps` lists background terminals when `unified_exec` is in use; otherwise the list may be empty.
Run `/ps` in the TUI to see each background terminal's command and recent output so you can tell whether it has finished.
Since v0.24.0, `write_stdin` can poll a running `session_id` while waiting for the command to finish.
Run `/ps` to see each background terminal's command and up to three recent non-empty output lines; it may be empty unless `unified_exec` is in use.
`/stop` stops all background terminals in the current session; `/clean` is its alias.
Since v0.24.0, `write_stdin` sends `chars` to a running `session_id`.
The agent asks for approval before terminal commands unless the configured run mode permits them.
Shell Mode uses `$SHELL`; zsh and bash are the documented supported shells.
The agent waits on a background command until it finishes or prints the output it is watching for.
Agent terminal calls run a shell non-interactively; `terminal.backend` selects local, Docker, SSH, or another documented backend.
`process_manage` with action `list` shows all background processes started via `terminal(background=true)`, and `poll` checks status plus new output for one.
Set `shell` in opencode.json. It selects the interactive terminal shell; compatible shells are also used for agent tool calls.
`pty.create` creates a PTY session for shell commands and processes and returns a session with an ID.
`pty.list` lists OpenCode-managed PTY sessions.
`pty.get` retrieves a PTY session, including its running or exited status and exit code.
`pty.remove` removes and terminates a specific PTY session.
`pty.connect` opens a WebSocket to interact with a running PTY session in real time.
The built-in `bash` tool runs with the permissions of the Pi process.
Use a `WebFetch(domain:...)` permission rule to allow, ask, or deny a host. Interactive 'don't ask again' approvals save a local allow rule.
Requires a supported Chromium browser, the Claude in Chrome extension, and `/login` with an eligible Anthropic plan.
Clicking runs through the Chrome extension; supported browser, extension, plan, and `/login` are required.
Typing and form filling run through the Chrome extension. Login pages and CAPTCHAs pause for manual handling.
Computer use and Chrome integration both let Claude take a screenshot and visually analyze it (e.g. to debug layout issues) as part of the same conversation.
Web search defaults to cached results. `--search` selects live search for a run; `web_search` controls the mode in config.
Attach a page screenshot with `--image` or `-i` for visual analysis; these records do not describe capturing the screenshot.
The agent uses the `Web` tool for searches; there is no separate search flag.
Fetches prompt for approval without an allowlist entry.
Runs through the Browser subagent; browser tool approval applies by default.
Runs through the Browser subagent; browser tool approval applies by default.
Runs through the Browser subagent; browser tool approval applies by default.
Browser logs are written to files the agent can inspect.
Screenshots can be read by the agent to inspect page layout and visual elements.
`web_search` uses a configured search backend; provider selection is under `web.*`.
`web_extract` returns readable page content and can also handle PDF URLs. Extraction backend and limits are configured under `web.*`.
Set `security.website_blocklist` in `config.yaml`; blocked domains return a policy error across web and browser tools.
Enable `computer_use` for CLI sessions. It requires cua-driver and OS permissions; vision-capable models can use screenshots, while text-only models use accessibility mode.
`websearch` requires the OpenCode or OpenCode Go provider, or a truthy `OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA` or `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL`.
Install `pi-web-access`; `web_search` uses a configurable provider fallback chain.
Install `pi-web-access`; `fetch_content` also handles GitHub URLs, PDFs and videos.
Install `pi-agent-browser-native` and put the upstream agent-browser binary on PATH.
Install `pi-agent-browser-native`; element references become invalid after navigation or restart.
Install `pi-agent-browser-native`; clicks can use page-scoped `@eN` references.
Install `pi-agent-browser-native`; form fills can use page-scoped `@eN` references.
Paste an image with `Ctrl+V` or pass it as an `@` file, for example `pi -p @screenshot.png "What's in this image?"`; the selected provider/model must accept image input.
Place Markdown agent definitions in `.claude/agents/` for a project or `~/.claude/agents/` for all projects; `--agents` supplies definitions as startup JSON.
Custom agent TOML files can set instructions, model, MCP servers, and skills. Place them in `~/.codex/agents/` or `.codex/agents/`; built-in tool allowlisting is not described.
Add a markdown file with YAML frontmatter in `.cursor/agents/` for the project or `~/.cursor/agents/` for the current user. Model choice can be limited by team settings or plan.
Set `mode: subagent` in the frontmatter. The V1 `opencode agent create` command is gone.
Since v0.24.0, the optional `subagent` example loads Markdown agent definitions with instructions, tools, and model.
`LSP` supports workspace symbol search when a language-specific code-intelligence plugin is installed; it is inactive in cloud sessions.
Configure `Stop` in the `hooks` settings object to run a handler when Claude finishes responding.
`/hooks` opens a view of configured hooks; hooks themselves are added or removed in settings files, plugins or frontmatter.
Writing `export` lines to the `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` path from a SessionStart, Setup, CwdChanged, or FileChanged hook persists environment variables for later Bash commands in the session.
A `Stop` hook can ask Codex to continue by returning a block decision with a reason.
`PostCompact` runs after manual or automatic compaction.
`/hooks` manages non-managed hooks; managed hooks are trusted by policy and cannot be disabled in the browser.
`shell_environment_policy.set = { KEY = "value" }` injects fixed environment variables into every spawned shell command, applied after exclusion filters.
Configure `stop` in `hooks.json`; a hook can submit a follow-up message when the agent loop ends. Automatic follow-ups have a per-script loop limit.
A `pre_verify` plugin hook fires when the agent is about to end its turn after editing code; returning a continue directive keeps it going, bounded by `agent.max_verify_nudges` (default 3).
A gateway hook (drop a handler.py + HOOK.yaml under ~/.hermes/hooks/) can subscribe to the `session:compress` event to run custom code right after context compaction finishes, in-place or rotated.
Manages shell-script hooks in `config.yaml`; `list` shows their status, and `revoke` clears consent entries on the next restart. Plugin hooks use a separate path.
Allowlist existing variables in `config.yaml` with `terminal.env_passthrough`, or declare them in skill frontmatter with `required_environment_variables`. Only set variables are forwarded.
A plugin can subscribe to the `session.idle` event to run custom logic (e.g. a notification) when the agent's turn/session completes.
Implement `shell.env` in a plugin; it applies to AI tool calls and user terminals.
Since v0.87.0, a `turn_end` handler can run at the end of a turn and return `continue: true` to request another provider turn.
Since v0.31.0, use `session_compact` to run extension logic after successful context compaction.
A trusted extension can handle `session_before_switch` and cancel the switch.
`/copy` copies the latest response. Add `[N]` to select an earlier one; code blocks open a picker. In iTerm2, `/terminal-setup` enables clipboard access.
Copies the latest completed output, including while a turn is running. Unavailable before the first completed output or immediately after a rollback.
`/copy [number]` copies the last assistant response (or the Nth-from-last) to the clipboard. CLI-only.
Run `/copy` in an interactive session to copy the last assistant message.
Attaches your terminal to a background session started with `claude --bg`; `claude logs <id>` and `claude stop <id>` manage it from the shell.
Requires a running app-server endpoint. Remote transport is experimental; use plain `ws://` only on localhost or through SSH port forwarding.
`agent persist list|stop` manages persistent sessions.
`hermes dashboard` opens the local dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`; its Chat tab provides browser chat. Embedded chat needs PTY support and WSL on Windows.
Browse reviewed MCP connectors in the Anthropic Directory (claude.ai/directory) and add any listed remote server with `claude mcp add`.
Reloads servers that come from plugins without restarting; use `--force` when the change would alter loaded tools.
Since v0.146.0, MCP connections update after authentication or configuration changes without restarting healthy connections.
Use `/reload-mcp` in the active session. MCP configuration also auto-reloads on running sessions, with a 30-second timeout.
With `pi-mcp-adapter` installed, use `/reload` after changing a server’s disabled setting to refresh its registered tools.
`video_generate` needs a configured video backend plugin and credential. `xai_video_edit` and `xai_video_extend` require xAI Imagine credentials.
Choose a provider with `hermes memory setup` or set `memory.provider`. One external provider can be active at a time; the built-in memory stores remain active alongside it.
Fast mode is a research preview for supported Opus models. It costs more per token and uses usage credits on subscriptions; it requires an Anthropic API or subscription connection.

Set `service_tier` for new turns, or use `/fast` in the interactive CLI when the active model advertises a Fast tier. Tier requests depend on model availability and do not guarantee latency or pricing.
`/fast` toggles Fast mode when the current model supports it; fast mode can carry higher rates.
Aliases are session-only by default; `--global` saves them in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
Since v2026.4.13, `/fast` selects priority processing for supported OpenAI and Anthropic models.
Since v0.67.0, configured `serviceTier` values select the OpenAI Codex serving tier; availability depends on the provider.
Updates the installed CLI to the latest version.
Shows plan usage limits and, on Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise, what counts against them; `/cost` and `/stats` are aliases.
Generates an HTML report from recent sessions on this machine; unavailable in cloud sessions.
`codex update` works when the installed release supports self-update. Debug builds require a release build; npm and Homebrew installs update through their package managers.
`/status` shows the percentage left in available plan limit windows; some accounts or providers may have no limit data.
Use `agent update` in the terminal or `/update` inside an interactive session.
`--check` checks without installing; `--plan` previews the update. Package-managed installs may be directed to their external updater.
`/usage` (or `hermes usage` outside a session) shows token/cost/session stats plus, when the provider supports it, an Account limits section with live remaining quota/credits/plan usage.
`hermes insights [--days N]` (or `/insights [days]`, default last 30 days) reports token, cost and activity analytics across recent sessions.
Pass an optional version target to install a specific version.
Limits of OpenCode Console and connected subscriptions.
`pi update --self` updates Pi only; `pi update --all` also updates packages.
`/goal` keeps the session working toward a condition across turns; `/goal clear` removes an active goal.
Requires the Claude Code GitHub Action (`anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`) in the repository; the trigger phrase is configurable.
`/goal` keeps a persistent task goal attached to the active chat across turns; it can set, inspect, edit, pause, resume, or clear that goal.
A Codex cloud feature on GitHub, not the CLI; needs the Codex GitHub app and code review enabled.
`/goal [objective]` gives the agent a standing objective it keeps pursuing until complete; the slash-commands table marks it 'Rolling out'.
`/goal <text>` continues across turns until the goal is done. It auto-pauses after 20 continuation turns by default; a new user message preempts the loop.
`acceptEdits` auto-approves file edits and common file commands; `bypassPermissions` skips prompts entirely and is meant for isolated environments.
Channels (research preview): Telegram/Discord bots pair with a code and default to allowlist-only senders; iMessage lets you add contacts by handle with `/imessage:access allow`.
A reviewer agent approves eligible low and medium-risk requests instead of prompting you; works with the on-request or granular approval policies.

`--force` (`-f`) allows commands unless explicitly denied; `--yolo` aliases it. `/run-everything`, `/auto-run`, or `approvalMode: unrestricted` select zero-prompt Run Everything. Team policy still applies.
YOLO skips dangerous-command approval prompts. `approvals.deny` and the hardline blocklist still apply; `/yolo` toggles the mode during a session.
Set global or platform user allowlists for gateway access. Approved DM pairing can also grant access; an explicit allow-all setting broadens access.
`--auto` approves requests that would otherwise ask; explicit deny rules still apply. It also has a TUI palette toggle.
Use `--resume` with a session ID or name and `--fork-session` to continue it under a new session ID.
`codex fork` opens a session picker by default; pass `SESSION_ID` to target one directly. The original transcript stays intact. `--all` includes sessions outside the current directory.
Pass the saved session’s ID to the `session.fork` API operation.
`--fork <path|id>` accepts a session file path or partial session ID.
`Monitor` feeds each output line to Claude while the command runs. Watches end after 5 minutes by default, up to 30 minutes, or 10 minutes in a non-interactive `-p` run.
Chrome integration drives your actual Chrome browser, so it inherits your existing logins (Gmail, Notion, Google Docs, etc.) with no separate profile setup.
Inspects page HTTP requests and responses. Browser docs place network traffic inspection in the Agent panel.
`browser.use_real_profile` snapshots your real Chrome/Brave/Edge profile (cookies, saved logins) so the agent browses as you; Browser Use Cloud also offers persistent cloud profiles.
Persistent profiles for authenticated sites come through `pi-agent-browser-native`; upstream `agent-browser` must be on PATH.
`--agent` runs a named subagent as the main session agent and overrides the persistent `agent` setting.
Set `color` in the subagent frontmatter.
Cursor cycles Agent, Plan, and Ask modes with `Shift+Tab` in the interactive CLI. `--plan`, `--mode=plan`, and `--mode=ask` select a mode at launch.
The Browser subagent uses MCP browser tools, which must be available in the session.
`color` changes UI color. `hidden: true` removes a subagent from @ autocomplete; agents can still invoke it through the Task tool.
Prefix a message with `&` to hand the live conversation to a Cloud Agent; pick it up at cursor.com/agents. Cloud access requires connected source control and repository read-write privileges.
Since v0.2.75, `@` file mentions add files to the conversation context; file suggestions remain available.
Set `disable-model-invocation: true` in a skill's `SKILL.md`, then invoke it with `/name`.
Claude can invoke a `SKILL.md` skill when its `description` fits the task.
These files apply across projects on the same machine.
Since v2.1.260, server-managed `claudeMd` supplies managed instructions; managed policy files still load for subagents.
Reads repository `AGENTS.md` as project instructions; added directories do not load their `AGENTS.md`.
Use `@` to include files or folders. A path written in the prompt is read when needed; it must exist and be accessible.
Set a project rule to Apply Manually, then mention that rule in chat.
A `.cursor/rules` project rule can use this type; the agent selects it from the rule description.
Define User Rules in Customize → Rules; they apply across projects.
Team and Enterprise plans can distribute these rules from the dashboard; admins can enforce them.
The CLI reads project-root `CLAUDE.md` and discovers skills in project or user Claude and Codex skill directories.
Use `@` to search workspace files, or `/mention` with a file or folder path. Both require an interactive session.
Set `policy.allow_implicit_invocation` to `false` in the skill’s `agents/openai.yaml` to require explicit `$skill` invocation.
Codex starts with skill names and descriptions, then loads the full `SKILL.md` when it chooses a matching skill.
Set `developer_instructions` in config.toml; it is injected as a developer-role message into every session.
Add names such as `CLAUDE.md` to read other agents’ instruction files; skill folders of other agents are not read.
Since v2026.8.3, `proactive_prune_tokens` can trigger automatic pruning of older tool results; it is off by default.
Invoke an installed skill with its slash command to load its `SKILL.md` instructions for that chat.
`USER.md` holds profile-local preferences and loads at session start when `memory.user_profile_enabled` is enabled.
Since v2026.8.3, `/init` inspects the project and generates or updates `AGENTS.md`.
Hermes detects `CLAUDE.md` and Cursor rules. Set `skills.external_dirs` to reuse a skills directory such as `~/.agents/skills`; specific agent skill directories are not auto-detected here.
Add a line range after the path, for example `@src/auth.ts#20-45`.
Configure aliases under `references`; `path` uses a local directory and `repository` uses Git. Git references refresh asynchronously. Use `@alias` for the root or `@alias/` for files.
Put instructions in a `SKILL.md` with a name and description; the agent can select and load it through `skill` when useful.
Use `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` for global rules, or set `instructions` in global configuration to include more files.
Skill folders made for other agents are read. `CLAUDE.md` is not: OpenCode 2 reads only `AGENTS.md`.
Type `@` to search project files in the editor, or pass an `@`-prefixed file as a CLI message argument.
Invoke a skill explicitly with `/skill:name`; skill commands are enabled by default.
The agent sees skill names and descriptions first, then reads the matching `SKILL.md` when needed.
Put `AGENTS.md` in `~/.pi/agent/` for global context; `CLAUDE.md` is a fallback. Global `SYSTEM.md` replaces the default prompt, while `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` appends to it.
Pi loads `CLAUDE.md` where `AGENTS.md` is absent.
`/skills` lists skills with type-to-filter and visibility controls.
Since v1.0.30, custom slash commands can insert Bash output and mentioned files into their prompts.
Set the GitHub Action `prompt` input to a skill invocation to run it in automation mode.
With `context: fork`, a skill starts a new subagent of the `agent` type in the background by default. It receives the skill content but no prior conversation history.
